name: Bay
grown_as: Sweet bay, an evergreen shrub or small tree, in gardens often a clipped bush or a standard in a pot. Male and female flowers are on separate plants: only females bear berries, and clipped plants may not flower. William's plant's sex is not known. ⚠️ CHECK
habit: A dense, upright evergreen shrub or small tree, usually kept 1 to 3 m but up to 10 m if left; smooth grey bark; young shoots green or reddish.

leaf.outline: Narrowly oval to lance-shaped, 5 to 10 cm long and 2 to 4 cm wide, widest about the middle
leaf.margin: Smooth, no teeth, often slightly wavy, with a thin pale edge
leaf.veins: A pale, raised midrib and fine side veins joined in a net, faint above
leaf.surface: Thick, stiff and leathery; glossy above, matt and paler beneath

flower.petals: Four small pale tepals (no true petals and sepals)
flower.centre: Male flowers have 8 to 12 stamens, making them fluffy; female flowers are smaller with a green ovary
flower.behind: Each small cluster sits in a cup of rounded bud scales
flower.carried: In small clusters of 4 to 6 in the leaf joints along the shoots, close to the stem, among the leaves

fruit: On female plants only: an oval berry 1 to 1.5 cm long, green ripening to glossy black in autumn, single or in small clusters in the leaf joints.
winter: Evergreen: unchanged, though hard frost and cold wind can brown the leaves.

leaf: a narrow oval leaf, pointed at both ends
smooth, often slightly wavy edge, no teeth
bloom: small creamy yellow fluffy flowers with four tepals and many stamens
in a small cluster in a leaf joint
young: a small upright shrub with glossy dark green leaves set singly
growing: a dense upright evergreen shrub or clipped bush
flower: small creamy yellow clusters tucked in the leaf joints all along the shoots

look_alikes: Cherry laurel is much larger in leaf, finely toothed, brighter green and poisonous: never cook with it. Portugal laurel has red stalks and finely toothed leaves. Spotted laurel (Aucuba) has coarsely toothed, often yellow-spotted leaves in opposite pairs.
